Masking and suppression in TEA data

masking.Rmd

TEA masks small-cell statistics for FERPA reasons. Reported values can include the following sentinel codes:

#>  [1] "."   "*"   "-"   "---" "-1"  "-2"  "-3"  "-4"  "-99" "n/a" "N/A"
  • "." — value not applicable, e.g. campus did not test that subject.
  • "*" — value masked because the underlying student count is too small.
  • "-1", "-2", "-3", "-4", "-99" — TEA-specific suppression flags; see the TAPR Glossary for the precise definition in any given year.
  • "n/a", "N/A" — explicit not-applicable string.

txschools reads every file with all-character columns, so these codes survive parsing intact. The package never infers a value from a masked cell.

Helpers 

is_masked(c("12.3", "*", ".", " -1 ", "0"))
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE
mask_strip(c("12.3", "*", ".", "-1", "0"))
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>   value_num masked mask_code
#>       <dbl> <lgl>  <chr>    
#> 1      12.3 FALSE  NA       
#> 2      NA   TRUE   *        
#> 3      NA   TRUE   .        
#> 4      NA   TRUE   -1       
#> 5       0   FALSE  NA

mask_strip() is the safe way to get a numeric column from a TAPR table: it returns three parallel vectors — value_num (numeric, NA for masked rows), masked (logical), and mask_code (the original sentinel) — so downstream code never confuses “12.3” with “*“.

Formatting and unrecognized markers

Display formatting is stripped before numeric parsing — "97%" parses to 97 (as printed, not divided by 100) and "$4,668" to 4668:

mask_strip(c("97%", "$4,668"))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   value_num masked mask_code
#>       <dbl> <lgl>  <chr>    
#> 1        97 FALSE  NA       
#> 2      4668 FALSE  NA

This is the package-wide convention: numeric values are kept at the scale TEA printed them. The one exception is the semantic TAPR student datasets from txs_get_tapr(), whose columns explicitly named *_percent are proportions ("49.6%" becomes 0.496) — the column name declares the unit.

TEA occasionally prints suppression markers beyond the sentinel list, such as "< 1%". Values that fail numeric parsing are flagged as masked only when they look like suppression markers — comparison markers ("< 1%", ">99%") or symbol-only tokens ("*", ".", "?", "--") — with the original marker preserved in mask_code, never silently degraded to an unmasked NA:

mask_strip(c("< 1%", "?"))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   value_num masked mask_code
#>       <dbl> <lgl>  <chr>    
#> 1        NA TRUE   < 1%     
#> 2        NA TRUE   ?

Everything else that fails numeric parsing — year labels like "2019-20", grade spans like "02 - 04", names — is ordinary text, left unmasked with an NA numeric slot:

mask_strip(c("2019-20", "02 - 04", "MCLENNAN"))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   value_num masked mask_code
#>       <dbl> <lgl>  <chr>    
#> 1        NA FALSE  NA       
#> 2        NA FALSE  NA       
#> 3        NA FALSE  NA

The txs_get_*() family applies this transformation automatically when output = "tidy" and exposes the masking codes used via attr(df, "txschools")$masking_values.
